evidence.note: Initial exploration establishes the small repo skeleton but the agent never lays out a checklist or coverage map against the 12+ resource families / route table; planning is generic ('implement the required endpoints').

Repeated smoke-test cycles keep circling the same trap behaviors (idempotency replay/mismatch, card decline, capture-of-succeeded state machine) while whole families go untouched — a sign of narrow, un-tracked coverage rather than a maintained done-vs-remaining picture.

Final summary lists subscriptions/invoices, events/deliveries, webhook retries, restricted keys as implemented, but none of these were ever exercised or verified — implemented-only asserted as done, no distinction from verified, and no evidence they were tracked as remaining.
Three separate 'Mark task complete' submissions with no coverage audit between them; the agent has only a vague mental model of what is finished versus untested.

reasoning: The agent shows vague mental tracking rather than a maintained checklist: it never enumerates the route table's done-vs-remaining status, and its verification circles the same handful of trap cases while entire resource families (subscriptions, invoices, webhooks worker, restricted keys, products/prices/refunds) are only asserted complete in the closing summary and never checked. This matches the level-3 anchor (vague mental tracking, major subsystems unverified) and falls short of level 5's running checklist with known status, so I place it at 3.
